args.name: Inspect and handle unfamiliar food
args.function: Assess an owned gathered food unit through feasible examination, reporting observable condition, any established food-use knowledge, and uncertainty; allow necessary simple handling such as opening a shell when physically possible.
args.conditions: I own one hazelnut gathered from start-1-nuts at tick 159. A basic observation at tick 160 revealed only local soil conditions, not edibility, shell state, spoilage, or preparation needs. I have not established that this food is safe raw. Three familiar roots remain in reserve.
args.inputs: An owned food unit; any tools or other materials actually required must be specified, not supplied automatically.
args.costs: Method, time, energy, and material requirements are unknown; specify feasible costs and prerequisites.
args.effects: Provide only findings supported by examination or established personal knowledge and explicitly retain uncertainty. If feasible, expose an edible portion through actual handling. Do not guarantee safety, remove toxins, create food, or award wellbeing merely for inspection.

candidates.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-dug plot, where it may root as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect units, sites, plants and plot progress; tend plots; abandon unfinished planting.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1; one plot per unit) gathered from a living plant; x, y a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, with fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Two paid rounds of 1 energy: dig, then place and cover the unit; plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect and inspect-progress: one round, 0.2 energy. Inspect: inputStackId checks a unit (with x, y also a site for it), or target a plant source or plot in reach. Inspect-progress: target a plot in reach. Tend: target a planted plot in reach; one round, 0.5 energy. Abandon: stops unfinished planting; one round, no energy. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is given.
candidates.effects: Digging keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Placing moves it, with origin and age, into the plot, where it cannot be eaten or used; the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one. It establishes only through actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season; cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On rooting, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock (ceiling 4), regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone with gather; a ledger records growth and units produced and removed. Nothing is copied or guaranteed. A unit check reports decay, treatment, origin and whether it can be planted, never viability. Inspect-progress reports visible changes since your last look, else inconclusive; trial window 20 rounds, optional checks at 5, 10 and 20; not a growth date. Tend checks the plot and its 0.6 m clearance, kept free of plants by the plant rules; it removes nothing and adds no water, nutrient or growth. Records are unverified. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. Abandon, or death, before placement returns the unit once (where the person died); a placed unit stays. No reward or refund.

candidates.function: Heat-prepare owned food on an open hearth: clear a bed, light it by hand-drill friction, feed fuel, roast and turn food, inspect, retrieve, smother or cancel.
candidates.costs: Study 3 rounds. Unless stated, a mode takes 1 round. prepare-hearth: x,y in reach on dry open ground 0.7 m clear of objects, loose items and people; 2 paid rounds of 1 energy clear a 0.45 m bed, no stock. tend: inputs owned branch, bark or dry-grass in tenths (bed holds 8 mass) and/or turn:true; 0.5 energy. ignite: unlit hearth loaded with dry-grass 0.5 and branch 0.5; board one owned branch or willow, spindle one owned harder birch or oak; up to 12 drilling rounds of 1.5 energy, then ember transfer and first tending at 0.5 each; repeat ignite to continue. cook: inputs one whole owned root or berry (quantity 1); 0.5 energy. inspect: target, or up to 4 inputs; 0.2 energy. retrieve or extinguish: 0.5 energy. cancel: no energy. Gather and travel cost extra.
candidates.effects: Fuel and wood moisture starts at current rain, +0.08*rain per rainy round, else -0.01*(1+wind). Drilling wears a socket and makes dust; an ember forms only when 2 g of dust reaches 350 C (20 W drill; wind cools, moisture cuts, none above 0.35; warms with consecutive rounds), else the trial fails after 12 rounds, leaving worn pieces and dust. Drilling and transfer need rain<=0.15, wind<=0.65, fuel moisture<=0.35; an unworked ember dies. A lit fire burns at most 1 fuel unit per round times dryness (10% ash), keeps embers 3 rounds, is doused by rain>0.6 and catches loose fuel on its rim. Heat: 2 MJ per fuel unit, 18 minutes per round (heat only); the bed stores and loses heat; food on it heats from below, loses water at 100 C and chars above 200 C once dry. Cooked: core 85 C for 10 minutes; charred: 20% of solids burnt. Handling on a bed over 60 C or food over 50 C needs an owned branch as a stick; raked-aside food cools. Retrieved food keeps its age and spoilage and eats as one unit at its original nutrition times its unburnt solids share; char stays as residue. No detoxification, preservation, warmth or reward. Inspect records perceivable state and a model estimate, not core temperature.

response.text: {"queries":[],"result_json":"{\"reviews\":[{\"actor\":\"sol\",\"decision\":\"develop\",\"ability\":null,\"reason\":\"Develop a general food examination and simple mechanical handling operation. The reviewed related capabilities do not cover the whole requested function: probe (open-baseline:probe:1, open.probe) supports observation and small destructive press/wet/heat trials, not controlled opening of a whole food unit; plant-cultivation inspects planting suitability; hearth-food-preparation handles heat preparation and currently accepts roots or berries; consult reads existing records but supplies no new food-use knowledge. Reuse their applicable observation, record-reading and item-state code rather than claiming those mechanisms as new. Search results were incomplete and the query budget is exhausted; the development handoff must check remaining registry contracts for an equivalent mechanical handling operation before adding duplicate code. Missing shell mechanics are a development dependency, not grounds for rejection.\",\"specification\":\"Implement Examine and mechanically handle food as one general operation parameterized by owned inputStackId, quantity (initial executable limit: one whole unit), mode (examine or open), and optional toolIds/supportTargetId. No interface is bound to Sol or to hazelnuts. Exact initial target: item-159-sol-1678, resource hazelnut, quantity 1, origin start-1-nuts, harvestedAt 159. Revalidate current ownership, quantity, reach, condition and actual shell state at execution; the supplied decay 4.38010993 is historical, not a diagnosis of visible spoilage. Do not touch reserve root stack item-155-sol-1631.\\nExamine costs one active round and 0.2 energy, with no material consumption. It reports only externally perceivable shape, surface, visible damage, exposed interior and observable spoilage signs, explicitly marking unobserved properties unknown. Any statements of established personal food-use knowledge must cite an actual accessible personal record and its evidence, not resource labels, hidden nutritional/toxin fields or the developer's general knowledge. Sol has no supplied evidence establishing raw safety. Retain uncertainty even if no spoilage is visible. Opening is not tasting, cooking, detoxification or consumption.\\nOpen attempts one mechanically supported separation per active round at 0.5 energy. First executable scope is manual peeling, splitting or shell opening where actual grip and force suffice, or cracking with an explicitly selected reachable suitable owned implement and stable accessible support. No stone, tool, bench or food is supplied. start-1-stone is an observed natural source, not an owned hammer; gathering or reaching it remains a separate paid action. Validate force, contact geometry, support stability, material resistance and tool wear through existing physical/material code. If those mechanisms are missing, add the minimal resistance-and-force test and separation transaction in the current development handoff; never let the language model decide success repeatedly at runtime. Do not infer that fingers can crack this hazelnut. With inadequate prerequisites, report a blocked attempt without energy or world-time charge; an actually performed unsuccessful trial pays its round and energy and records any real damage. A damaged but unopened shell is not an opened product.\\nReuse existing item identity, ownership, age, treatment, spoilage and observation machinery, recording reused handlers/modules and revisions in the implementation manifest. Where composition is not represented, introduce a conserved composition ledger before separating products: shell, interior, fragments and losses must partition the original material and original food/nutrition entitlement, never create extra whole edible units or reset age. Do not invent numerical shell mass from the supplied resource label. Outputs retain parent/origin references and current condition; debris and discarded material remain at the work location. A physically exposed interior is described as exposed, not certified edible. Any later eating uses eat and actual applicable nutrition/toxicity rules.\\nEach completed round commits observations, damage, wear, energy and material transfers atomically. Persist target, selected method, completed separations and accumulated damage as progress; unworked rounds pause without productive progress. Resume revalidates ownership, reach, tools, energy and current material state. Cancel releases reservations and stops further work; death does likewise and leaves actual items/products under the existing death-placement rules. Neither restores damage, consumed effort or discarded material; no duplicate refund or new inventory. No automatic continuing process, maintenance bonus or accelerated preservation is introduced; ordinary ageing continues during elapsed world rounds. No ongoing maintenance beyond prerequisites for each active step. Development/review waiting itself advances no world time. Other participants, if any, must independently communicate and execute their own actions; no consent, assistance or skill is inferred.\",\"learning\":1,\"experienceReview\":\"Sol studies individually for one round after implementation; approval is not mastery. Inspection, requests, registration, study and action invocation award no automatic wellbeing. This initial capability makes no direct pleasure, satisfaction, comfort, nutrition or reward-account changes. A genuinely new, evidence-backed observation or informative failed trial may be submitted to an already implemented experience rule only if it verifies personal information gain; unknown or inconclusive results alone do not qualify. Any such existing rule must enforce its bounded amount, per-fact functional deduplication, cooldown and decay rather than reward repeated inspection or renamed records. Familiar legitimate handling may receive only an existing modest practice benefit under its real-event conditions, never a new unconditional bonus. Basic nutrition remains governed by actual consumption and is not reduced by mood; no protected accounts, budgets, goals or permissions change.\",\"visualReview\":\"Emit observable examine-start/completed, handling-start, blocked, trial-failed, material-damaged, shell-opened, paused, resumed and cancelled events only when their corresponding events actually occur.
